 Going ahead, the Fed’s policy decision next week will be the key trigger, with the rate outlook and policy guidance likely to determine gold’s near-term direction, 
 Dipen Pradhan 
 October 26, 2026 / 09:10 IST Share -->

 --> 
 Gold Prices Across India on October 26 Gold prices edged down to just above $3,999 per ounce.
 Fed policy decision and US inflation data remain key focus.
 MCX gold futures for Dec 4 inched to Rs 1,42,451 per 10g.

 Gold price edged 0.07 percent down just above $3,999 per ounce in the early session on October 26, while US gold futures declined 0.22 percent to $3,999.10 per ounce (02:09 GMT) from its previous close.
 MCX gold futures for December 4 delivery inched 0.03 percent to Rs 1,42,451 per 10 grams from its previous close, and silver 0.55 percent to Rs 1,96,803 per kilogram (09:05 IST). Domestic MCX spot gold closed Friday (Oct. 23) at Rs 1,41,031 per 10 grams, and silver at Rs 1,94,170 per kilogram, from their previous closes.
 "Higher rate expectations and elevated bond yields continue to weigh on bullion by increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. Going ahead, the Fed’s policy decision next week will be the key trigger, with the rate outlook and policy guidance likely to determine gold’s near-term direction," Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities, said.

 "Gold prices steadied near $4,000 after falling more than 4 percent last week and briefly slipping below the psychological level for the first time since July, as elevated energy prices continued to weigh on the monetary-policy outlook. Brent gained more than 6 percent last week amid persistent Middle East supply risks, reinforcing concerns that higher energy costs could keep US inflation elevated and limit the Fed’s flexibility. However, crude prices eased in early trade amid renewed diplomatic efforts, providing some relief to bullion," Manav Modi, Commodities Analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said.
 The 10-year Treasury yield remained near 5 percent, weighing on bullion, although continued geopolitical uncertainty provided underlying safe-haven support. Attention now shifts toward the Fed’s October 27–28 meeting, where markets widely expect rates to remain unchanged, making Chair Warsh’s guidance on the December meeting particularly important. Markets currently price in around a 78 percent probability of a December hike following stronger CPI and PPI readings.
 "PCE inflation later this week will therefore remain another crucial trigger, with any upside surprise likely to reinforce tightening expectations, while softer inflation could provide relief to gold," Modi said.
